My cousin tried to go find our families’ ties to Positano, Italy during her honeymoon around the Mediterranean. Sadly it seems most of that side has either moved away or passed on (I vaguely remember meeting my grandmother’s cousins from over there once).
I also have some Irish heritage on my mom’s side, but trying to trace the old records of where my great-grandmother was from just hit a wall (records were lost), so I settled on just visiting Dublin… in February. Man, I get it it was cold and got dark fast, but most of the people we met were kinda grumpy. Honestly we met like three nice folks, an old shopkeeper selling made in Ireland stuff, the morning waitress in our hotel restaurant and the taxi driver that took us back to the airport. (We came in on the ferry from Wales after visiting London.)

comments.author: @rkt7414
comments.text:
10:24 I am going to Daegu in 3 hours!
 
I live in Korea up in Seongnam-si with my wife (I'm American, she's Korean) for 2½ years now. 

At the tourism center counter inside the Incheon Airport train station they give out these Korean Heritage Site passport booklets, there's 76 locations dotted around the country and if you visit each one and stamp the corresponding pages in your book, you'll get an appreciation plaque from the government thanking you for your fondness of Korean culture. The book for Korean nationals is blue, the book for foreigners is red.

Separately from this, earlier this summer they released a limited edition special silver-colored passport in commemoration of the UNESCO Heritage commission holding their 48th session in Busan. It's a much more limited list of 30 locations, but it has a deadline of November 30th. There is some overlap between the main 76 and the 30 special locations but some are exclusive to the UNESCO list and the stamp stations for these locations will be removed after November 30th. Also nobody knows what the reward will be for completing it, because the period of time during which you can submit the booklet is Dec 1st~13th, meaning by the time anybody knows what the reward is, it'll be too late to complete it if you haven't already. 

I have 6 locations left, all in the area surrounding Daegu.

I look forward to seeing the historic sites your mom might've gotten to see on school field trips! I'll check out that espresso cafe you recommended. See if you can grab one of those passport booklets on your next trip into the country! You can chip away at the list of locations with every successive visit

replies.author: @rkt7414
replies.text:
Also for the record it is 1:50 in the morning (of Saturday, Nov 28th) and I was being serious when I said I was going there in 3 hours. My train leaves from Suseo to Dong-Daegu at 5:30 and I'll probably have to wake up and leave the house at 4 to catch the bus to the station.

I'm getting like NO sleep tonight.
